newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up on India/Egypt talk, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up on India/Egypt talk, weather.

text.p: Talk that India this week is in the market for 50,000 to 750,000 tonnes of wheat, an Egyptian tender plus concerns about dry weather in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region boosted CBOT wheat futures to a higher close, traders said.
"India will be in tonight for wheat. They're saying 50,000 but it could be up to 750,000 tonnes, it's an open-ended tender," a trader said.
U.S. exporters said India Tuesday would seek 50,000 tonnes or more of optional-origin wheat for March shipment. The wheat will come from either Australia or the U.S., they said.
Also there was talk India found problems with the quality of some Canadian wheat shipments. But India's State Trading Corporation denied that scenario existed.
A Canadian Wheat Board (CWB) spokesman told Reuters the CWB is not aware of any problems with Canadian wheat destined for India.
Traders also cited talk Egypt this week may be in the market for a large quantity of wheat on the world market.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 to three cents per bushel higher, with March up 1-1/2 at $3.73. May was three cents higher at $3.59 and July was up three at $3.47-1/4.

A Cairo report early Tuesday noted Egypt would be seeking 50,000 tonnes of Argentina, U.S. or French wheat for loading in March or April. But market rumblings held that Egypt later this week may buy from 400,000 to 800,000 tonnes of wheat.
"They could buy any amount from 400,000 to 800,000 tonnes," a trader said.

In the background of export talk was news of Sri Lanka's tender for 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat. That tender was slated for February 6 and one U.S. exporter said 50,000 tonnes would be soft wheat and the other 50,000 tonnes would be hard wheat.
Key players were Tenco Inc with 1.5 million bushels purchased in the March and Cargill Inc bought one million March, traders said.
E.D. and F. Man International sold two million bushels of March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, above the 9,429 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought 600 March $3.70 puts at 6-1/2 cents and bought 600 March $3.60 puts at 2-3/4 cents, traders said. Prudential Securities sold 600 May $3.60 calls at 13-1/4 to 14-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,000 contracts, above the 5,648 traded Monday.
